inputs.prompt:
<Picture 1> is the authoritative spatial map of the world, not a visual-style reference. Treat it as a top-down geometric specification of a Yuanmingyuan-style imperial garden park in Beijing: tree-lined gravel paths, a big ornamental lake with lotus leaves, white-marble ruins blocks of the Western Mansions, stone balustrades, a narrow stone causeway, Chinese pavilions in the distance, summer daylight. Do not imitate the appearance of the map; infer plausible 3D terrain and architecture.

FIRST-PERSON BICYCLE CAMERA, non-negotiable: shot from a camera mounted on the bicycle's handlebar at exactly 1.6 meters above the ground, looking straight ahead horizontally. The handlebar grips and both of the rider's hands holding them are ALWAYS VISIBLE at the bottom edge of the frame, in every frame. The ground surface fills the lower half of the image; trees, walls and balustrades pass at eye level; the horizon stays near the middle of the frame. The camera NEVER rises above 1.6 m, NEVER looks down at the ground from above. Absolutely NO aerial view, NO drone shot, NO bird's-eye view, NO top-down or map-like overview.

Camera timeline (total 5.2 seconds, 24 fps), riding at cycling speed:
- 0.0s-2.0s: ride straight north along the tree-lined gravel path; the lake is on your LEFT.
- 2.0s-4.0s: at the stone plaza junction, turn LEFT by 90 degrees at constant smooth rate onto the stone causeway that crosses the lake.
- 4.0s-5.2s: ride straight along the causeway with lake water on BOTH sides of the view.
The left turn is MANDATORY: the heading at 5.2s must point 90 degrees left of the 0s heading, all at 1.6 m height with the handlebar in frame.
